exercise1.prompt: A list of records is a table waiting to happen.

hiddenCases.name: a key only some records have still becomes a column
pandas builds the table
hiddenCases.describe: a DataFrame built from the records

exercise1.hint: pd.DataFrame takes the list of dictionaries directly. sorted(df.columns) then gives plain strings in a predictable order.

questions.prompt: A JSON list of objects maps onto a table how?
questions.explain: Each object is a record, and its keys are the columns. That is why API responses drop straight into a DataFrame.

questions.prompt: One record is missing the "score" key. What happens?
choices: That row gets a missing value in the score column
questions.explain: The table is the union of all keys, and any record without one simply has a gap there.

questions.prompt: Why not just read the first record's keys to learn the columns?
choices: Later records can carry keys the first one does not
questions.explain: The first row is not a schema. Any record can introduce a column, which is exactly what the hidden case in the exercise checks.
